heard: This deep blue world 64 light years away holds no peaceful oceans. When French astronomers discovered HD 189,733 b in October 2005, its azure shade seemed familiar. Most people imagine water, but this planet is a scorching gas giant larger than Jupiter. Titly locked to its parent star, atmospheric temperatures reach roughly 1,200 Kelvin. The cobalt color is actually caused by high-altitude haze scattering light. Those clouds are composed of silicates, the exact mineral family of glass and sand. Powerful jet streams blow these tiny silicate particles sideways across the planet. To make matters worse, the lethal atmosphere reeks like rotten eggs from hydrogen sulfide.
